1	"""Promotion of normalized signals into the triage queue.
2	
3	``persist_signals`` stores every signal a sync sees; this module decides which of
4	them are work and writes those as ``WorkItem`` rows, so the queue the GUI renders
5	is no longer empty after a sync.
6	
7	The decision is one function, :func:`should_promote`, and it is deliberately
8	rule-based: no LLM, no network, no stored state. The same signal always decides the
9	same way, which is what lets the heuristic be scored against a labeled sample of
10	real mail and corrected by hand when it gets one wrong.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import re
16	from collections.abc import Collection
17	from typing import Any
18	
19	from pydantic import HttpUrl, TypeAdapter, ValidationError
20	from sqlalchemy import select
21	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
22	
23	from ..models import Source, SourceKind, SourcePromotion, WorkItem
24	from ..schemas import EvidenceInput, WorkItemCreate
25	from .graph import parse_observed_at
26	from .work_items import create_work_item
27	
28	# Matched against the local part with separators removed, so ``no-reply@``,
29	# ``no_reply@`` and ``noreply-github@`` are all the same address shape.
30	AUTOMATED_SENDER_MARKERS = ("noreply", "donotreply", "autoreply", "mailerdaemon", "postmaster",
31	                            "bounce", "newsletter", "marketing", "campaign", "mailinglist")
32	BULK_HEADERS = ("list-unsubscribe", "list-id", "list-post", "x-campaign-id")
33	PRECEDENCE_HEADER = "precedence"
34	AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER = "auto-submitted"
35	BULK_PRECEDENCE = frozenset({"bulk", "list", "junk"})
36	# Every header name ``_is_bulk_mail`` looks at, lowercased, derived from the names the
37	# rule itself uses so the two cannot drift apart. ``persist_signals`` stores these and
38	# discards the rest of Graph's header block: a name no rule reads is message metadata
39	# kept on disk for nothing.
40	HEURISTIC_HEADERS = frozenset(BULK_HEADERS) | {PRECEDENCE_HEADER, AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER}
41	
42	TITLE_LIMIT = 500
43	# The same bound ``persist_signals`` puts on ``Source.excerpt``; the evidence copy
44	# is the same text and should not be able to grow past it.
45	EXCERPT_LIMIT = 2_000
46	FALLBACK_TITLE = "(no subject)"
47	
48	# The same validator ``WorkItemCreate.source_url`` applies; a link it would reject
49	# (wrong scheme, no host, over 2083 characters) is dropped rather than truncated,
50	# because a truncated URL is a wrong one.
51	_HTTP_URL = TypeAdapter(HttpUrl)
52	
53	
54	def _local_part(sender: str) -> str:
55	    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", sender.split("@", 1)[0].lower())
56	
57	
58	def _is_automated_sender(sender: str | None) -> bool:
59	    return bool(sender) and any(marker in _local_part(str(sender)) for marker in AUTOMATED_SENDER_MARKERS)
60	
61	
62	def _is_bulk_mail(headers: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
63	    lowered = {str(name).lower(): str(value).strip().lower() for name, value in headers.items()}
64	    if any(header in lowered for header in BULK_HEADERS):
65	        return True
66	    if lowered.get(PRECEDENCE_HEADER) in BULK_PRECEDENCE:
67	        return True
68	    return lowered.get(AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER, "no") != "no"
69	
70	
71	def _is_only_copied(signal: dict[str, Any], owner_addresses: Collection[str]) -> bool:
72	    """True when the owner is known, there is a To list, and none of the owner's addresses is in it."""
73	    recipients = signal.get("to_recipients") or []
74	    owners = {address.strip().lower() for address in owner_addresses}
75	    if not owners or not recipients:
76	        return False
77	    return owners.isdisjoint(str(address).strip().lower() for address in recipients)
78	
79	
80	def should_promote(signal: dict[str, Any], owner_addresses: Collection[str] = ()) -> bool:
81	    """Decide whether one normalized signal belongs in the triage queue.
82	
83	    The rules, in order; the first that matches decides:
84	
85	    1. Skip anything posted by an application rather than a person. A Teams bot
86	       relaying build output is not work addressed to anybody.
87	    2. Skip an automated sender -- a local part carrying ``noreply``, ``donotreply``,
88	       ``autoreply``, ``mailer-daemon``, ``postmaster``, ``bounce``, ``newsletter``,
89	       ``marketing``, ``campaign`` or ``mailinglist``, compared with separators
90	       removed so punctuation cannot dodge the rule. The domain is not consulted:
91	       a person at a marketing agency is still a person.
92	    3. Skip bulk mail identified by the headers a mass mailing is obliged to carry:
93	       ``List-Unsubscribe``, ``List-Id``, ``List-Post``, ``X-Campaign-Id``,
94	       ``Precedence: bulk|list|junk``, or an ``Auto-Submitted`` other than ``no``.
95	       Leaning on headers is what lets rule 2 stay short and leave ``info@``,
96	       ``news@`` and ``updates@`` -- addresses real people also write from -- alone.
97	    4. Skip mail the owner was only copied on: the owner is known, the message
98	       carries a To list, and none of the owner's addresses is in it. Cc is an FYI,
99	       not a request. Teams messages carry no To list, so this rule cannot reject them.
100	    5. Otherwise promote: it reached the owner's own mailbox or chat, from a person.
101	
102	    ``owner_addresses`` are the signed-in user's own addresses -- both the principal
103	    name and the mail address, since alias-domain tenants hand out different ones.
104	    Without any, rule 4 is skipped rather than guessed at, so a missing profile
105	    costs recall, never silence.
106	    """
107	    if signal.get("sender_kind") == "application":
108	        return False
109	    if _is_automated_sender(signal.get("sender")):
110	        return False
111	    if _is_bulk_mail(signal.get("headers") or {}):
112	        return False
113	    return not _is_only_copied(signal, owner_addresses)
114	
115	
116	def _source_url(value: object) -> HttpUrl | None:
117	    """Keep a source URL only when ``HttpUrl`` accepts it; one bad link must not abort the sync."""
118	    try:
119	        return _HTTP_URL.validate_python(str(value))
120	    except ValidationError:
121	        return None
122	
123	
124	def _work_item(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> WorkItemCreate:
125	    """Build the create payload, carrying the message excerpt across as evidence."""
126	    kind = SourceKind(str(signal["source_kind"]))
127	    external_id = str(signal["external_id"])
128	    return WorkItemCreate(
129	        title=(str(signal.get("title") or "").strip() or FALLBACK_TITLE)[:TITLE_LIMIT],
130	        source_kind=kind,
131	        source_external_id=external_id,
132	        source_url=_source_url(signal.get("source_url")),
133	        evidence=[EvidenceInput(
134	            source_kind=kind,
135	            external_id=external_id,
136	            excerpt=str(signal.get("excerpt") or "")[:EXCERPT_LIMIT] or None,
137	            observed_at=parse_observed_at(signal.get("observed_at")),
138	        )],
139	    )
140	
141	
142	def _record_considered(db: Session, external_id: str) -> None:
143	    """Record that promotion judged this signal's stored ``Source``, whatever it decided.
144	
145	    Written for rejections as much as for promotions: a rejected ``Source`` is the
146	    one case ``work_items`` cannot describe on its own, and without this row the
147	    backfill in ``app/services/backfill.py`` would read it as a source promotion
148	    had never seen and promote it after all.
149	
150	    Only a stored source can be recorded. ``promote_signals`` is also called with
151	    signals whose ``Source`` row was never written -- by the unit tests in
152	    ``tests/test_promotion.py``, and by any future caller that promotes without
153	    persisting -- and those have nothing for the backfill to reconsider anyway.
154	    """
155	    source_id = db.scalar(select(Source.id).where(Source.external_id == external_id))
156	    if source_id is not None and db.get(SourcePromotion, source_id) is None:
157	        db.add(SourcePromotion(source_id=source_id))
158	
159	
160	def promote_signals(db: Session, signals: list[dict[str, Any]], owner_addresses: Collection[str] = ()) -> int:
161	    """Create a pending work item for every actionable signal; return how many are new.
162	
163	    Idempotent through ``work_items.source_external_id``: a signal already promoted
164	    is skipped, so re-running a sync over the same inbox window adds nothing and the
165	    unique constraint is never reached.
166	
167	    Every signal whose source is stored is also recorded as judged (see
168	    ``_record_considered``), so the backfill can later tell a source this function
169	    rejected from one it was never shown. That record is committed here rather than
170	    left to whatever ``create_work_item`` happens to commit: a batch that rejects
171	    every signal never calls ``create_work_item`` at all, and without an explicit
172	    commit here the judged-rows it added would be discarded when the caller's
173	    session closes, silently reopening the door this table exists to close.
174	    """
175	    created = 0
176	    for signal in signals:
177	        external_id = str(signal["external_id"])
178	        _record_considered(db, external_id)
179	        if not should_promote(signal, owner_addresses):
180	            continue
181	        if db.scalar(select(WorkItem.id).where(WorkItem.source_external_id == external_id)) is not None:
182	            continue
183	        create_work_item(db, _work_item(signal))
184	        created += 1
185	    db.commit()
186	    return created

1	"""One-off promotion of ``Source`` rows that were stored before promotion existed.
     2	
     3	``persist_signals`` has been writing ``Source`` rows since the first release, but
     4	the heuristic that turns them into work items arrived later. Those earlier rows
     5	were never offered to it, so the queue the GUI renders stays empty for them until
     6	something offers them once. That is all this module does.
     7	
     8	**How it picks rows, and why not the obvious way.** The tempting predicate is
     9	"every ``Source`` with no matching ``WorkItem``". It is wrong: a source the
    10	heuristic deliberately rejected also has no matching work item, so that predicate
    11	drags every newsletter and no-reply message back into the queue on the first run
    12	that finds anything to promote. This module instead selects on the absence of a
    13	``SourcePromotion`` row, which ``promote_signals`` writes for every signal it
    14	judges, either verdict. Absence of that row is the one fact that means "promotion
    15	has never decided about this source".
    16	
    17	**Where it runs.** From ``POST /api/sync/backfill`` only, behind the same
    18	``require_local_write_access`` guard as ``POST /api/sync``. Not from application
    19	startup: ``main.py`` deliberately touches no table at boot
    20	(``tests/test_migrations.py::test_application_startup_writes_no_schema_of_its_own``
    21	pins that), and a startup hook querying ``sources`` would raise against a database
    22	whose migrations have not run yet -- exactly the state that test runs against.
    23	Because it is never on the boot path, boot speed on an empty database is not a
    24	property this module has to hold; nothing here runs until an operator calls the
    25	endpoint.
    26	
    27	**What "considered" can and cannot mean.** A never-judged ``Source`` is fed to the
    28	same :func:`should_promote` a live sync uses, so it always reaches a verdict;
    29	nothing here can fail to answer. But two things make that verdict weaker than the
    30	one a live sync reaches, and the response counts each of them separately rather
    31	than presenting a run as a clean decision.
    32	
    33	*No stored context.* A genuinely pre-promotion row carries no
    34	``SourceSignalContext`` -- ``sender``, ``sender_kind``, ``to_recipients`` and
    35	``headers`` were never asked for before that table existed -- so on it rules 1-4
    36	have nothing to read and only rule 5 can fire: it is promoted unconditionally.
    37	That is a permanent data gap, not a bug, and the contract's answer to it is the
    38	owner's manual dismiss (T08), not a second heuristic guessing a sender from a
    39	subject line. ``judged_without_context`` counts these rows, so an operator knows
    40	which promotions in a run were a real decision and which were a coin that only
    41	ever lands heads.
    42	
    43	*No owner addresses.* Rule 4 skips mail the owner was only copied on, and it needs
    44	the owner's own addresses to do that. They exist only in the live Graph profile a
    45	sync fetches (``sync._owner_addresses``); nothing persists them and no setting
    46	supplies them, so this module has none to pass and **rule 4 never fires here, on
    47	any row**. Mail the owner was merely copied on is therefore promoted by the
    48	backfill even though a live sync declines it. ``promoted_without_owner_check``
    49	counts the promotions this actually puts at risk -- rows that carried a To list
    50	and got past rules 1-3, so rule 4 was the one remaining rule that could have said
    51	no. A positive count is a list of rows worth reviewing, not a failed run; closing
    52	the gap for real needs a durable record of the owner's addresses, which does not
    53	exist anywhere in this application yet.
    54	"""
    55	
    56	from __future__ import annotations
    57	
    58	from typing import Any
    59	
    60	from sqlalchemy import select
    61	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
    62	
    63	from ..models import Source, SourcePromotion
    64	from .promotion import promote_signals, should_promote
    65	
    66	
    67	def _signal_from_source(source: Source) -> dict[str, Any]:
    68	    """Rebuild the normalized signal shape from what the row actually kept.
    69	
    70	    A ``Source`` written after ``SourceSignalContext`` existed carries its real
    71	    sender, sender kind, recipients and headers, and those are included here so
    72	    rules 1-3 of ``should_promote`` can genuinely decide -- treating a source that
    73	    has this data as if it did not would silently downgrade every backfill to
    74	    rule 5, which is exactly the bug the permanent-gap paragraph above describes
    75	    for rows that truly lack it. Rule 4 is not in that list: it is unreachable
    76	    here whatever this function returns, for want of owner addresses.
    77	    ``to_recipients`` is still carried across, because it is what
    78	    :func:`_promoted_without_owner_check` reads to tell a promotion rule 4 might
    79	    have overturned from one it could not have. A source with no context row omits
    80	    the four keys entirely, so ``should_promote`` reads them as unknown through
    81	    ``.get()`` instead of being handed an invented sender or an empty header block
    82	    that could be mistaken for "checked and clean".
    83	    """
    84	    signal: dict[str, Any] = {
    85	        "external_id": source.external_id,
    86	        "source_kind": source.kind.value,
    87	        "title": source.subject,
    88	        "excerpt": source.excerpt,
    89	        "source_url": source.url,
    90	        "observed_at": source.observed_at.isoformat(),
    91	    }
    92	    context = source.signal_context
    93	    if context is not None:
    94	        signal["sender"] = context.sender
    95	        signal["sender_kind"] = context.sender_kind
    96	        signal["to_recipients"] = context.to_recipients or []
    97	        signal["headers"] = context.headers or {}
    98	    return signal
    99	
   100	
   101	def _promoted_without_owner_check(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   102	    """True when this signal is promoted only because rule 4 had no owner addresses to check.
   103	
   104	    Rule 4 can reject a signal only if it reaches it -- one rules 1-3 let through
   105	    -- and only if there is a To list to look in: ``_is_only_copied`` returns
   106	    ``False`` on an empty one, so a Teams message or a mail with no recipients is
   107	    decided identically whether or not the owner is known. Asking
   108	    ``should_promote`` itself, with the same empty ``owner_addresses`` the backfill
   109	    passes to ``promote_signals``, keeps that rule ordering in the single function
   110	    that owns it instead of restating the rules here.
   111	    """
   112	    return bool(signal.get("to_recipients")) and should_promote(signal)
   113	
   114	
   115	def backfill_promoted_sources(db: Session) -> dict[str, int]:
   116	    """Offer every never-judged ``Source`` to the heuristic once; report what happened.
   117	
   118	    Safe to re-run: ``promote_signals`` records each source it judges, so a second
   119	    call selects nothing and every count in the response is 0. Re-running is the
   120	    expected operator path, not an edge case -- the endpoint is a button, and
   121	    buttons get pressed twice.
   122	
   123	    The response never collapses to a single number, because a single
   124	    ``new_work_items`` count cannot say which of four very different situations
   125	    happened: nothing was left to judge (``considered`` is 0); something was judged
   126	    and none of it was actionable (``considered`` is positive, ``new_work_items`` is
   127	    0); some of what was judged could not be judged on its merits at all, for lack
   128	    of stored context (``judged_without_context`` is positive) and its verdict is a
   129	    guess, not a decision; or something was promoted with rule 4 unavailable
   130	    (``promoted_without_owner_check`` is positive), which a live sync might have
   131	    declined. The last two count different rows and neither implies the other: a
   132	    context-less row is never counted as an owner-check miss, because rule 4 would
   133	    have had no recipients to read on it either.
   134	    """
   135	    unjudged = list(db.scalars(
   136	        select(Source)

"""Local bearer/session access and CSRF protections for Workboard.

The bearer token is a local-host trust boundary, not a defense against a
compromised host, browser profile, or Docker daemon. It is separate from and
must never be reused as a Microsoft Graph credential.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import secrets
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from threading import Lock
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Cookie, Depends, Header, HTTPException, status

from .config import Settings, get_settings

SESSION_COOKIE = "workboard_session"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LocalAccess:
    via_bearer: bool
    csrf_token: str | None = None
    session_id: str | None = None


_sessions: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
_sessions_lock = Lock()


def _configured_token(settings: Settings) -> str:
    configured = settings.local_api_token
    expected = configured.get_secret_value() if configured else ""
    if not expected:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
            detail="LOCAL_API_TOKEN must be configured before accessing Workboard data",
        )
    return expected


def _valid_bearer(authorization: str | None, expected: str) -> bool:
    scheme, _, supplied = (authorization or "").partition(" ")
    return scheme.lower() == "bearer" and bool(supplied) and hmac.compare_digest(supplied, expected)


def require_local_agent_token(authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None,
                              settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> None:
    """Authenticate an installed agent directly with the local bearer token."""
    if not _valid_bearer(authorization, _configured_token(settings)):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
                            detail="A valid local API bearer token is required",
                            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})


def create_browser_session(settings: Settings) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return an opaque session id and CSRF token; neither is persisted to disk."""
    session_id, csrf_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32), secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    with _sessions_lock:
        _sessions[session_id] = (csrf_token, time.monotonic() + settings.local_session_ttl_seconds)
    return session_id, csrf_token


def clear_browser_session(session_id: str | None) -> None:
    if session_id:
        with _sessions_lock:
            _sessions.pop(session_id, None)


def _session_csrf(session_id: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not session_id:
        return None
    with _sessions_lock:
        stored = _sessions.get(session_id)
        if not stored:
            return None
        csrf_token, expires_at = stored
        if expires_at <= time.monotonic():
            _sessions.pop(session_id, None)
            return None
        return csrf_token


def require_local_access(authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None,
                         session_id: Annotated[str | None, Cookie(alias=SESSION_COOKIE)] = None,
                         settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> LocalAccess:
    """Allow either an installed-agent bearer token or an opaque browser session."""
    expected = _configured_token(settings)
    if authorization:
        if _valid_bearer(authorization, expected):
            return LocalAccess(via_bearer=True)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="A valid local API bearer token is required",
                            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    csrf_token = _session_csrf(session_id)
    if csrf_token:
        return LocalAccess(via_bearer=False, csrf_token=csrf_token, session_id=session_id)
    raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="A local browser session or bearer token is required",
                        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})


def require_local_write_access(access: LocalAccess = Depends(require_local_access),
                               csrf_token: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="X-CSRF-Token")] = None) -> LocalAccess:
    """Cookie-authenticated writes require CSRF; direct bearer calls do not."""
    if not access.via_bearer and (not csrf_token or not hmac.compare_digest(csrf_token, access.csrf_token or "")):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="A valid X-CSRF-Token header is required")
    return access

---
"""index the columns the list endpoints filter and sort on

``GET /api/work-items`` and ``GET /api/sources`` filter on ``WorkItem.status``,
``WorkItem.source_kind`` and ``Source.kind``, and sort on ``WorkItem.updated_at``
and ``Source.observed_at`` -- none of them indexed, so every page scans the whole
table. ``Source.external_id`` already carries an index implicitly through its
unique constraint (``0001``), so it is not repeated here.

Index names match exactly what SQLAlchemy's default naming produces for
``index=True`` on these columns (``ix_<table>_<column>``), because a database
built by ``Base.metadata.create_all`` -- the pre-Alembic startup path, and the
legacy fixture in ``tests/test_migrations.py`` -- already carries indexes under
those names. ``upgrade`` skips a name it finds already present rather than
failing on a duplicate, the same posture ``0004``/``0005`` take for their tables.

Revision ID: 0006
Revises: 0005
Create Date: 2026-09-18 13:13:56.020505
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import context, op

revision: str = '0006'
down_revision: str | None = '0005'
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None

# (index name, table, column)
INDEXES: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (
    ("ix_work_items_status", "work_items", "status"),
    ("ix_work_items_source_kind", "work_items", "source_kind"),
    ("ix_work_items_updated_at", "work_items", "updated_at"),
    ("ix_sources_kind", "sources", "kind"),
    ("ix_sources_observed_at", "sources", "observed_at"),
)


def _existing_index_names() -> frozenset[str]:
    """Index names already on disk, empty for an offline (``--sql``) run."""
    if context.is_offline_mode():
        return frozenset()
    inspector = sa.inspect(op.get_bind())
    names: set[str] = set()
    for table in {table for _, table, _ in INDEXES}:
        names.update(index["name"] for index in inspector.get_indexes(table))
    return frozenset(names)


def upgrade() -> None:
    present = _existing_index_names()
    for name, table, column in INDEXES:
        if name in present:
            continue
        op.create_index(name, table, [column])


def downgrade() -> None:
    for name, table, _ in INDEXES:
        op.drop_index(name, table_name=table)

1	"""Pagination and indexes for the two list endpoints.
2	
3	``GET /api/work-items`` and ``GET /api/sources`` used to return every row with no
4	limit, so the response grew without bound as the queue did. These tests hold the
5	envelope shape shut at the FastAPI boundary -- not just in the service helper --
6	because a helper that paginates correctly proves nothing about a route that never
7	calls it with the caller's numbers, and hold the migration's indexes shut against
8	a real ``alembic upgrade head`` database, because an ``index=True`` in
9	``app.models`` that never reaches a revision is invisible to a test that only
10	inspects ``Base.metadata``.
11	
12	Every fixture here is synthetic; no real mail content lives in this repository.
13	"""
14	
15	import os
16	import subprocess
17	import sys
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
21	from sqlalchemy import create_engine, inspect
22	
23	from app.main import app
24	from app.services.work_items import DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT, MAX_PAGE_LIMIT
25	
26	BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
27	TOKEN_HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
28	
29	
30	def _create_work_item(client: TestClient, index: int, status: str = "pending") -> dict:
31	    payload = {
32	        "title": f"Work item {index}",
33	        "source_kind": "manual",
34	        "source_external_id": f"manual:item-{index}",
35	        "status": status,
36	    }
37	    # status is not settable on create; set it via a follow-up PATCH so the fixture
38	    # can still exercise the status filter.
39	    created = client.post("/api/work-items", json={k: v for k, v in payload.items() if k != "status"},
40	                          headers=TOKEN_HEADERS)
41	    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text
42	    item = created.json()
43	    if status != "pending":
44	        patched = client.patch(f"/api/work-items/{item['id']}", json={"status": status}, headers=TOKEN_HEADERS)
45	        assert patched.status_code == 200, patched.text
46	        item = patched.json()
47	    return item

51	    created = client.post("/api/sources", json={"kind": kind, "external_id": f"{kind}:source-{index}"},

147	        for i in range(5):
148	            _create_source(client, i)
149	
150	        response = client.get("/api/sources", params={"limit": 2, "offset": 1}, headers=TOKEN_HEADERS)
151	
152	        assert response.status_code == 200
153	        body = response.json()
154	        assert set(body.keys()) == {"items", "total", "limit", "offset"}
155	        assert body["total"] == 5
156	        assert len(body["items"]) == 2
157	        assert body["limit"] == 2

161	def _run_with_database(database_path: Path, *argv: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
162	    environment = {**os.environ, "DATABASE_URL": f"sqlite:///{database_path}"}
163	    return subprocess.run(
164	        [sys.executable, *argv],

166	        env=environment,
167	        capture_output=True,
168	        text=True,
169	        timeout=25,

174	    database_path = tmp_path / "indexed.db"
175	
176	    result = _run_with_database(database_path, "-m", "alembic", "upgrade", "head")

180	    try:

1	"""Promotion of ``Source`` rows that were stored before promotion existed.
2	
3	``persist_signals`` has written ``Source`` rows since the first release; promotion
4	only arrived later. Those earlier rows were never offered to the heuristic, so the
5	queue stays empty for them until a backfill offers them once.
6	
7	The whole difficulty is that "never offered" is not the same as "offered and
8	declined", and ``work_items`` cannot tell the two apart on its own -- both leave a
9	``Source`` with no matching ``WorkItem``. A selection predicate of "every source
10	with no work item" therefore re-promotes exactly the newsletters and no-reply mail
11	the heuristic deliberately threw away (blocked twice, attempt 1), and a queue-level
12	gate that stops once anything has ever been promoted silently disables the
13	backfill forever after the first ordinary sync (blocked twice, attempt 2).
14	``source_promotions`` is the row that breaks the tie, written by ``promote_signals``
15	for every signal it judges, either verdict; the tests below hold each of those
16	failure shapes shut, built -- where the fixture matters -- through the real
17	writers, ``persist_signals`` and ``promote_signals``, rather than bare ``Source``
18	rows, because only a source the heuristic has genuinely seen and turned down can
19	catch attempt 1's bug.
20	
21	Every fixture here is synthetic; no real mail content lives in this repository.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	from datetime import datetime
27	from typing import Any
28	
29	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
30	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
31	
32	from app.database import engine
33	from app.main import app
34	from app.models import Source, SourceKind, SourcePromotion, WorkItem, WorkStatus
35	from app.services.backfill import backfill_promoted_sources
36	from app.services.graph import persist_signals
37	from app.services.promotion import promote_signals
38	
39	MAILBOX = "owner@contoso.com"
40	OWNER = (MAILBOX,)
41	BEARER = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
42	
43	# Distinctive enough that finding it on a work item cannot be a coincidence.
44	MARKER = "backfilled-excerpt-marker-91c4ae"
45	
46	
47	def _stored_source(external_id: str, subject: str, excerpt: str = MARKER) -> Source:
48	    """A ``Source`` exactly as a pre-promotion release left it: no context, no ledger row."""
49	    return Source(
50	        kind=SourceKind.outlook_email,
51	        external_id=external_id,
52	        subject=subject,
53	        url="https://outlook.office.com/mail/" + external_id,
54	        excerpt=excerpt,

56	    )

62	        "external_id": "outlook:direct-1",
63	        "source_kind": "outlook_email",

65	        "excerpt": MARKER,

67	        "observed_at": "2026-09-18T08:30:00Z",

88	def test_backfill_promotes_a_source_stored_before_promotion_existed() -> None:
89	    """AC8: a row the heuristic was never given a chance to judge gets one."""
90	    with Session(engine) as session:
91	        session.add(_stored_source("outlook:legacy-1", "Can you review the migration plan?"))
92	        session.commit()

95	
96	        assert result == {"considered": 1, "new_work_items": 1, "judged_without_context": 1, "promoted_without_owner_check": 0}
97	        item = session.query(WorkItem).one()
98	        assert item.source_external_id == "outlook:legacy-1"
99	        assert item.status == WorkStatus.pending
100	        assert item.evidence[0].excerpt == MARKER

103	def test_backfill_leaves_a_source_the_live_heuristic_declined_unpromoted() -> None:

"""initial schema

Baseline: exactly the schema the old ``Base.metadata.create_all`` startup hook
produced. A ``workboard.db`` that predates Alembic already holds these tables and
carries no ``alembic_version`` row, so ``upgrade`` skips creation when every one
of them is present with the columns declared below, and only records the revision.
Every later change belongs in a new revision; this one changes only if the schema
it has to recognise was misdescribed.

Revision ID: 0001
Revises: 
Create Date: 2026-09-18 01:46:46.258258
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

from alembic import context, op
import sqlalchemy as sa

revision: str = '0001'
down_revision: str | None = None
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None


# Exactly what the ``create_table`` calls below produce. The skip check needs its
# own record of that, because it must keep recognising a pre-Alembic database long
# after later revisions have moved ``app.models`` away from this shape.
# ``tests/test_migrations.py`` fails if this stops matching the DDL beside it.
BASELINE_COLUMNS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    "sources": frozenset({
        "id", "kind", "external_id", "subject", "url", "excerpt", "observed_at",
        "created_at", "updated_at",
    }),
    "work_items": frozenset({
        "id", "title", "summary", "status", "priority", "source_kind",
        "source_external_id", "source_url", "assigned_agent", "due_at", "created_at",
        "updated_at",
    }),
    "agent_dispatches": frozenset({
        "id", "work_item_id", "client", "instruction", "status", "result",
        "created_at", "updated_at",
    }),
    "work_evidence": frozenset({
        "id", "work_item_id", "source_kind", "external_id", "excerpt", "observed_at",
    }),
}


def _column_drift(inspector: sa.Inspector) -> list[str]:
    """How the database's baseline tables differ from this revision's, as prose."""
    drift: list[str] = []
    for table, expected in BASELINE_COLUMNS.items():
        present = {column["name"] for column in inspector.get_columns(table)}
        if missing := expected - present:
            drift.append(f"{table} is missing {sorted(missing)}")
        if unexpected := present - expected:
            drift.append(f"{table} has unexpected {sorted(unexpected)}")
    return drift


def _baseline_already_present() -> bool:
    """True for a database the pre-Alembic ``create_all`` startup already built.

    Offline (``--sql``) runs have no database to inspect and always emit the full
    DDL. A database that only half matches -- missing some of the tables, or holding
    a baseline table whose columns were altered afterwards -- was never left by
    ``create_all``. Stamping one would strand the difference forever, since no later
    revision recreates what this one skipped, so it is refused instead.
    """
    if context.is_offline_mode():
        return False
    inspector = sa.inspect(op.get_bind())
    existing = BASELINE_COLUMNS.keys() & set(inspector.get_table_names())
    if not existing:
        return False
    if existing != BASELINE_COLUMNS.keys():
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"database holds only {sorted(existing)} of the baseline tables; "
            "repair it by hand before migrating"
        )
    if drift := _column_drift(inspector):
        raise RuntimeError(
            "database holds every baseline table but " + "; ".join(drift) + "; "
            "repair it by hand before migrating"
        )
    return True


def upgrade() -> None:
    if _baseline_already_present():
        return
    op.create_table('sources',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('kind', sa.Enum('outlook_email', 'teams_message', 'manual', name='sourcekind'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('external_id', sa.String(length=512), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('subject', sa.String(length=500), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('url', sa.String(length=2048), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('excerpt', sa.Text(), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('observed_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('created_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('updated_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id'),
    sa.UniqueConstraint('external_id')
    )
    op.create_table('work_items',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('title', sa.String(length=500), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('summary', sa.Text(), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('status', sa.Enum('pending', 'in_progress', 'blocked', 'done', name='workstatus'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('priority', sa.Enum('low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent', name='workpriority'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('source_kind', sa.Enum('outlook_email', 'teams_message', 'manual', name='sourcekind'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('source_external_id', sa.String(length=512), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('source_url', sa.String(length=2048), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('assigned_agent', sa.String(length=128), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('due_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('created_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('updated_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id'),
    sa.UniqueConstraint('source_external_id')
    )
    op.create_table('agent_dispatches',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('work_item_id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('client', sa.String(length=32), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('instruction', sa.Text(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('status', sa.Enum('queued', 'delivered', 'completed', 'failed', name='dispatchstatus'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('result', sa.Text(), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('created_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('updated_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(['work_item_id'], ['work_items.id'], ondelete='CASCADE'),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
    )
    op.create_table('work_evidence',
    sa.Column('id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('work_item_id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('source_kind', sa.Enum('outlook_email', 'teams_message', 'manual', name='sourcekind'), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('external_id', sa.String(length=512), nullable=False),
    sa.Column('excerpt', sa.Text(), nullable=True),
    sa.Column('observed_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),
    sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(['work_item_id'], ['work_items.id'], ondelete='CASCADE'),
    sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint('id')
    )


def downgrade() -> None:
    op.drop_table('work_evidence')
    op.drop_table('agent_dispatches')
    op.drop_table('work_items')
    op.drop_table('sources')

1	"""Promotion of normalized signals into the triage queue.
     2	
     3	``persist_signals`` stores every signal a sync sees; this module decides which of
     4	them are work and writes those as ``WorkItem`` rows, so the queue the GUI renders
     5	is no longer empty after a sync.
     6	
     7	The decision is one function, :func:`should_promote`, and it is deliberately
     8	rule-based: no LLM, no network, no stored state. The same signal always decides the
     9	same way, which is what lets the heuristic be scored against a labeled sample of
    10	real mail and corrected by hand when it gets one wrong.
    11	"""
    12	
    13	from __future__ import annotations
    14	
    15	import re
    16	from collections.abc import Collection
    17	from typing import Any
    18	
    19	from pydantic import HttpUrl, TypeAdapter, ValidationError
    20	from sqlalchemy import select
    21	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
    22	
    23	from ..models import Source, SourceKind, SourcePromotion, WorkItem
    24	from ..schemas import EvidenceInput, WorkItemCreate
    25	from .graph import parse_observed_at
    26	from .work_items import create_work_item
    27	
    28	# Matched against the local part with separators removed, so ``no-reply@``,
    29	# ``no_reply@`` and ``noreply-github@`` are all the same address shape.
    30	AUTOMATED_SENDER_MARKERS = ("noreply", "donotreply", "autoreply", "mailerdaemon", "postmaster",
    31	                            "bounce", "newsletter", "marketing", "campaign", "mailinglist")
    32	BULK_HEADERS = ("list-unsubscribe", "list-id", "list-post", "x-campaign-id")
    33	PRECEDENCE_HEADER = "precedence"
    34	AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER = "auto-submitted"
    35	BULK_PRECEDENCE = frozenset({"bulk", "list", "junk"})
    36	# Every header name ``_is_bulk_mail`` looks at, lowercased, derived from the names the
    37	# rule itself uses so the two cannot drift apart. ``persist_signals`` stores these and
    38	# discards the rest of Graph's header block: a name no rule reads is message metadata
    39	# kept on disk for nothing.
    40	HEURISTIC_HEADERS = frozenset(BULK_HEADERS) | {PRECEDENCE_HEADER, AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER}
    41	
    42	TITLE_LIMIT = 500
    43	# The same bound ``persist_signals`` puts on ``Source.excerpt``; the evidence copy
    44	# is the same text and should not be able to grow past it.
    45	EXCERPT_LIMIT = 2_000
    46	FALLBACK_TITLE = "(no subject)"
    47	
    48	# The same validator ``WorkItemCreate.source_url`` applies; a link it would reject
    49	# (wrong scheme, no host, over 2083 characters) is dropped rather than truncated,
    50	# because a truncated URL is a wrong one.
    51	_HTTP_URL = TypeAdapter(HttpUrl)
    52	
    53	
    54	def _local_part(sender: str) -> str:
    55	    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", sender.split("@", 1)[0].lower())
    56	
    57	
    58	def _is_automated_sender(sender: str | None) -> bool:
    59	    return bool(sender) and any(marker in _local_part(str(sender)) for marker in AUTOMATED_SENDER_MARKERS)
    60	
    61	
    62	def _is_bulk_mail(headers: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    63	    lowered = {str(name).lower(): str(value).strip().lower() for name, value in headers.items()}
    64	    if any(header in lowered for header in BULK_HEADERS):
    65	        return True
    66	    if lowered.get(PRECEDENCE_HEADER) in BULK_PRECEDENCE:
    67	        return True
    68	    return lowered.get(AUTO_SUBMITTED_HEADER, "no") != "no"
    69	
    70	
    71	def _is_only_copied(signal: dict[str, Any], owner_addresses: Collection[str]) -> bool:
    72	    """True when the owner is known, there is a To list, and none of the owner's addresses is in it."""
    73	    recipients = signal.get("to_recipients") or []
    74	    owners = {address.strip().lower() for address in owner_addresses}
    75	    if not owners or not recipients:
    76	        return False
    77	    return owners.isdisjoint(str(address).strip().lower() for address in recipients)
    78	
    79	
    80	def should_promote(signal: dict[str, Any], owner_addresses: Collection[str] = ()) -> bool:
    81	    """Decide whether one normalized signal belongs in the triage queue.
    82	
    83	    The rules, in order; the first that matches decides:
    84	
    85	    1. Skip anything posted by an application rather than a person. A Teams bot
    86	       relaying build output is not work addressed to anybody.
    87	    2. Skip an automated sender -- a local part carrying ``noreply``, ``donotreply``,
    88	       ``autoreply``, ``mailer-daemon``, ``postmaster``, ``bounce``, ``newsletter``,
    89	       ``marketing``, ``campaign`` or ``mailinglist``, compared with separators
    90	       removed so punctuation cannot dodge the rule. The domain is not consulted:
    91	       a person at a marketing agency is still a person.
    92	    3. Skip bulk mail identified by the headers a mass mailing is obliged to carry:
    93	       ``List-Unsubscribe``, ``List-Id``, ``List-Post``, ``X-Campaign-Id``,
    94	       ``Precedence: bulk|list|junk``, or an ``Auto-Submitted`` other than ``no``.
    95	       Leaning on headers is what lets rule 2 stay short and leave ``info@``,
    96	       ``news@`` and ``updates@`` -- addresses real people also write from -- alone.
    97	    4. Skip mail the owner was only copied on: the owner is known, the message
    98	       carries a To list, and none of the owner's addresses is in it. Cc is an FYI,
    99	       not a request. Teams messages carry no To list, so this rule cannot reject them.
   100	    5. Otherwise promote: it reached the owner's own mailbox or chat, from a person.
   101	
   102	    ``owner_addresses`` are the signed-in user's own addresses -- both the principal
   103	    name and the mail address, since alias-domain tenants hand out different ones.
   104	    Without any, rule 4 is skipped rather than guessed at, so a missing profile
   105	    costs recall, never silence.
   106	    """
   107	    if signal.get("sender_kind") == "application":
   108	        return False
   109	    if _is_automated_sender(signal.get("sender")):
   110	        return False
   111	    if _is_bulk_mail(signal.get("headers") or {}):
   112	        return False
   113	    return not _is_only_copied(signal, owner_addresses)
   114	
   115	
   116	def _source_url(value: object) -> HttpUrl | None:
   117	    """Keep a source URL only when ``HttpUrl`` accepts it; one bad link must not abort the sync."""
   118	    try:
   119	        return _HTTP_URL.validate_python(str(value))
   120	    except ValidationError:
   121	        return None
   122	
   123	
   124	def _work_item(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> WorkItemCreate:
   125	    """Build the create payload, carrying the message excerpt across as evidence."""
   126	    kind = SourceKind(str(signal["source_kind"]))
   127	    external_id = str(signal["external_id"])
   128	    return WorkItemCreate(
   129	        title=(str(signal.get("title") or "").strip() or FALLBACK_TITLE)[:TITLE_LIMIT],
   130	        source_kind=kind,
   131	        source_external_id=external_id,
   132	        source_url=_source_url(signal.get("source_url")),
   133	        evidence=[EvidenceInput(
   134	            source_kind=kind,
   135	            external_id=external_id,
   136	            excerpt=str(signal.get("excerpt") or "")[:EXCERPT_LIMIT] or None,
   137	            observed_at=parse_observed_at(signal.get("observed_at")),
   138	        )],
   139	    )
   140	
   141	
   142	def _record_considered(db: Session, external_id: str) -> None:
   143	    """Record that promotion judged this signal's stored ``Source``, whatever it decided.
   144	
   145	    Written for rejections as much as for promotions: a rejected ``Source`` is the
   146	    one case ``work_items`` cannot describe on its own, and without this row the
   147	    backfill in ``app/services/backfill.py`` would read it as a source promotion
   148	    had never seen and promote it after all.
   149	
   150	    Only a stored source can be recorded. ``promote_signals`` is also called with
   151	    signals whose ``Source`` row was never written -- by the unit tests in
   152	    ``tests/test_promotion.py``, and by any future caller that promotes without
   153	    persisting -- and those have nothing for the backfill to reconsider anyway.
   154	    """
   155	    source_id = db.scalar(select(Source.id).where(Source.external_id == external_id))
   156	    if source_id is not None and db.get(SourcePromotion, source_id) is None:
   157	        db.add(SourcePromotion(source_id=source_id))
   158	
   159	
   160	def promote_signals(db: Session, signals: list[dict[str, Any]], owner_addresses: Collection[str] = ()) -> int:
   161	    """Create a pending work item for every actionable signal; return how many are new.
   162	
   163	    Idempotent through ``work_items.source_external_id``: a signal already promoted
   164	    is skipped, so re-running a sync over the same inbox window adds nothing and the
   165	    unique constraint is never reached.
   166	
   167	    Every signal whose source is stored is also recorded as judged (see
   168	    ``_record_considered``), so the backfill can later tell a source this function
   169	    rejected from one it was never shown. That record is committed here rather than
   170	    left to whatever ``create_work_item`` happens to commit: a batch that rejects
   171	    every signal never calls ``create_work_item`` at all, and without an explicit
   172	    commit here the judged-rows it added would be discarded when the caller's
   173	    session closes, silently reopening the door this table exists to close.
   174	    """
   175	    created = 0
   176	    for signal in signals:
   177	        external_id = str(signal["external_id"])
   178	        _record_considered(db, external_id)
   179	        if not should_promote(signal, owner_addresses):
   180	            continue
   181	        if db.scalar(select(WorkItem.id).where(WorkItem.source_external_id == external_id)) is not None:
   182	            continue
   183	        create_work_item(db, _work_item(signal))
   184	        created += 1
   185	    db.commit()
   186	    return created

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app


def test_work_item_evidence_context_and_dispatch_round_trip():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        token_headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
        created = client.post(
            "/api/work-items",
            json={
                "title": "Reply to the customer",
                "summary": "Confirm the delivery date.",
                "source_kind": "outlook_email",
                "source_external_id": "message-123",
                "evidence": [{"source_kind": "outlook_email", "external_id": "message-123", "excerpt": "Can you confirm?"}],
            }, headers=token_headers,
        )
        assert created.status_code == 201
        work_item = created.json()
        assert work_item["evidence"][0]["external_id"] == "message-123"

        context = client.post("/api/agent-context", json={"work_item_id": work_item["id"], "client": "codex"}, headers=token_headers)
        assert context.status_code == 200
        assert "Can you confirm?" in context.json()["prompt"]

        dispatch = client.post(
            "/api/agent-dispatches",
            json={"work_item_id": work_item["id"], "client": "codex", "instruction": "Draft a concise reply."}, headers=token_headers,
        )
        assert dispatch.status_code == 201
        assert dispatch.json()["status"] == "queued"


def test_validation_and_duplicate_source_external_id_are_rejected():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
        invalid = client.post("/api/work-items", json={"title": "", "source_kind": "manual", "unexpected": True}, headers=headers)
        assert invalid.status_code == 422

        payload = {"title": "Unique source", "source_kind": "teams_message", "source_external_id": "chat-unique"}
        assert client.post("/api/work-items", json=payload, headers=headers).status_code == 201
        assert client.post("/api/work-items", json=payload, headers=headers).status_code == 409

     2	
     3	import atexit
     4	import os
     5	import shutil
     6	import tempfile
     7	
     8	# ``app.database`` builds its engine at import time from an ``@lru_cache``d
     9	# ``get_settings()``, so ``DATABASE_URL`` has to be set before any test module
    10	# imports application code -- a session-scoped ``tmp_path_factory`` fixture would
    11	# run long after collection has already imported ``app.database``. Choosing the
    12	# directory here, at conftest import time, gives every pytest process its own
    13	# SQLite file, so parallel runs cannot drop each other's tables.
    14	_TEST_DB_DIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="workboard-tests-")
    15	atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, _TEST_DB_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
    16	os.environ["DATABASE_URL"] = f"sqlite:///{_TEST_DB_DIR}/workboard-tests.db"
    17	os.environ["LOCAL_API_TOKEN"] = "test-local-agent-token"
    18	
    19	# Message content lives in encrypted columns (``Source.excerpt``,
    20	# ``WorkEvidence.excerpt``) and every write of one fails closed without a key, so
    21	# the suite has to be configured the way a deployment is. A key generated per
    22	# pytest process keeps this out of the repository and out of any other run; the
    23	# tests that assert the keyless 503 delete the variable again through monkeypatch.
    24	from app.services.crypto import generate_encryption_key
    25	
    26	os.environ["APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY"] = generate_encryption_key()

    35	def _clear_session_store() -> None:
    36	    """Empty the module-level browser session store through its own lock.
    37

    39	    keeps every module that already imported the object in sync with it.

    41	    with _sessions_lock:
    42	        _sessions.clear()

    47	    """Give every API test a fresh schema and uncached environment settings.
    48	
    49	    The schema is built with ``create_all`` rather than by running the Alembic
    50	    chain. A per-test ``drop_all`` + ``upgrade head`` would leave a stale
    51	    ``alembic_version`` row behind and cost far more than it proves: API tests
    52	    that pass against ``create_all`` but whose author forgot to add a revision
    53	    would still pass, because both mechanisms read the same ``app.models``.
    54	    ``tests/test_migrations.py`` covers the real risk instead -- it applies the
    55	    chain to an empty database and asserts the result has not drifted from the
    56	    metadata -- so the two mechanisms cannot silently disagree.
    57	    """
    58	    get_settings.cache_clear()
    59	    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
    60	    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    61	    _clear_session_store()
    62	    yield

    64	    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)

"""record which sources the promotion heuristic has judged

Adds ``source_promotions``, one row per ``Source`` promotion has already decided
about. The backfill in ``app/services/backfill.py`` selects on the absence of that
row, because ``work_items`` cannot distinguish a source the heuristic rejected from
one it was never shown, and promoting the first kind is the defect this table
exists to prevent.

**The table is created empty, on purpose.** An existing ``Source`` row is then read
as never judged, so the first backfill offers it to the heuristic -- which is the
behaviour AC8 asks for, and the reason this revision does not stamp the rows it
finds. Stamping them all would be the safer-looking choice and would make the
backfill a no-op on precisely the databases it was written for.

That leaves one window: rows written by a build that already promoted on sync but
predates this table would be indistinguishable from pre-promotion rows, and their
rejects would be promoted once. The window is empty in practice -- promotion and
this table are unreleased work reaching an installation in the same deployment, so
no release ever promoted without recording it -- and it is bounded to a single
backfill run even if that ever stopped being true. An operator who did run the
in-between build can close it by hand before backfilling, by inserting a row here
for every source that build saw.

A new table cannot be confused with the pre-Alembic schema revision ``0001``
recognises: that check reads only the four baseline tables and their columns, and
this one is not among them. It is skipped when already present for the same reason
``0001`` skips -- a database built by ``Base.metadata.create_all`` already has it.

Revises: 0004
Create Date: 2026-09-18 22:10:00.000000
"""

import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import context, op

revision: str = '0005'
down_revision: str | None = '0004'
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None

TABLE = "source_promotions"


def _already_present() -> bool:
    """True for a database ``create_all`` already built this table in.

    Offline (``--sql``) runs have nothing to inspect and always emit the DDL.
    """
    return not context.is_offline_mode() and TABLE in sa.inspect(op.get_bind()).get_table_names()


def upgrade() -> None:
    if _already_present():
        return
    op.create_table(
        TABLE,
        sa.Column('source_id', sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
        sa.Column('considered_at', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),

"""index the columns the list endpoints filter and sort on

``GET /api/work-items`` and ``GET /api/sources`` filter on ``WorkItem.status``,
``WorkItem.source_kind`` and ``Source.kind``, and sort on ``WorkItem.updated_at``
and ``Source.observed_at`` -- none of them indexed, so every page scans the whole
table. ``Source.external_id`` already carries an index implicitly through its
unique constraint (``0001``), so it is not repeated here.

Index names match exactly what SQLAlchemy's default naming produces for
``index=True`` on these columns (``ix_<table>_<column>``), because a database
built by ``Base.metadata.create_all`` -- the pre-Alembic startup path, and the
legacy fixture in ``tests/test_migrations.py`` -- already carries indexes under
those names. ``upgrade`` skips a name it finds already present rather than
failing on a duplicate, the same posture ``0004``/``0005`` take for their tables.

Revision ID: 0006
Revises: 0005
Create Date: 2026-09-18 13:13:56.020505
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import context, op

revision: str = '0006'
down_revision: str | None = '0005'
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None

# (index name, table, column)
INDEXES: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (
    ("ix_work_items_status", "work_items", "status"),
    ("ix_work_items_source_kind", "work_items", "source_kind"),
    ("ix_work_items_updated_at", "work_items", "updated_at"),
    ("ix_sources_kind", "sources", "kind"),
    ("ix_sources_observed_at", "sources", "observed_at"),
)


def _existing_index_names() -> frozenset[str]:
    """Index names already on disk, empty for an offline (``--sql``) run."""
    if context.is_offline_mode():
        return frozenset()
    inspector = sa.inspect(op.get_bind())
    names: set[str] = set()
    for table in {table for _, table, _ in INDEXES}:
        names.update(index["name"] for index in inspector.get_indexes(table))
    return frozenset(names)


def upgrade() -> None:
    present = _existing_index_names()
    for name, table, column in INDEXES:
        if name in present:
            continue
        op.create_index(name, table, [column])


def downgrade() -> None:
    for name, table, _ in INDEXES:
        op.drop_index(name, table_name=table)

``should_promote`` gets it wrong sometimes -- a real inbox is not a fixture -- and
the owner needs two ways to correct it by hand: promote a ``Source`` the rules
missed, and dismiss a ``WorkItem`` that should never have been promoted.

Dismissing is a status transition, never a delete (B36 already pins the hand
-delete path as a permanent rejection; this is the other one). The status must
survive both places a source could otherwise be offered to the heuristic again --
an ordinary re-sync through ``promote_signals`` and the T06 backfill through
``backfill_promoted_sources`` -- so each has its own test rather than one that
only proves the API route flips a column.

Promoting by hand must also write the same ``source_promotions`` ledger row
``promote_signals`` writes (B44), or the backfill would read the source as never
judged and offer it to the heuristic again, reporting a promotion this endpoint
already made.

Every fixture here is synthetic; no real mail content lives in this repository.

from uuid import UUID

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.database import engine
from app.main import app
from app.models import SourcePromotion, WorkItem, WorkStatus

def dismiss_work_item(db: Session, item_id: UUID) -> WorkItem:
    """Hand-correct a wrongly-promoted item without deleting it (T08, AC10).

    A status transition, not ``delete_work_item``: ``promote_signals`` and the T06
    backfill (``app/services/backfill.py``) both treat "no ``WorkItem`` row for this
    ``source_external_id``" as "never promoted", so a hard delete would let either
    one recreate this item on the very next re-sync. Leaving the row in place --
    under a status neither of those two paths ever offers for repromotion -- is
    what makes a dismissal stick.
    """
    item = get_work_item(db, item_id)
    item.status = WorkStatus.dismissed
    db.commit()
    return get_work_item(db, item.id)

    """Promote a ``Source`` by hand, overriding whatever ``should_promote`` decided (T08, AC10).

    This is the owner's correction for the heuristic's false negatives: a source
    ``promote_signals`` rejected, or one it has not judged at all yet. Neither
    :func:`should_promote` nor ``owner_addresses`` are consulted -- the owner
    looking at the message is the decision here, not the heuristic.

    Writes the same ``SourcePromotion`` ledger row :func:`_record_considered`
    would have written on a live judgement (B44). Without it, this source would
    still read as "never judged" to ``app.services.backfill.backfill_promoted_sources``,
    which would offer it to the heuristic again and report a promotion this
    endpoint already made.

    already exists -- promoted, dismissed, or otherwise -- the same conflict
    ``create_work_item`` would hit against the ``source_external_id`` unique
    constraint, raised earlier so nothing is written first.

    if db.scalar(select(WorkItem.id).where(WorkItem.source_external_id == source.external_id)) is not None:

+"""Hand correction of the promotion heuristic (T08, AC10).
+
+``should_promote`` gets it wrong sometimes -- a real inbox is not a fixture -- and
+the owner needs two ways to correct it by hand: promote a ``Source`` the rules
+missed, and dismiss a ``WorkItem`` that should never have been promoted.
+
+Dismissing is a status transition, never a delete (B36 already pins the hand
+-delete path as a permanent rejection; this is the other one). The status must
+survive both places a source could otherwise be offered to the heuristic again --
+an ordinary re-sync through ``promote_signals`` and the T06 backfill through
+``backfill_promoted_sources`` -- so each has its own test rather than one that
+only proves the API route flips a column.
+
+Promoting by hand must also write the same ``source_promotions`` ledger row
+``promote_signals`` writes (B44), or the backfill would read the source as never
+judged and offer it to the heuristic again, reporting a promotion this endpoint
+already made.
+
+Every fixture here is synthetic; no real mail content lives in this repository.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from app.database import engine
+from app.main import app
+from app.models import SourcePromotion, WorkItem, WorkStatus
+from app.services.backfill import backfill_promoted_sources
+from app.services.graph import persist_signals
+from app.services.promotion import promote_signals
+
+MAILBOX = "owner@contoso.com"
+OWNER = (MAILBOX,)
+BEARER = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
+
+
+def _email(**overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """A normalized inbox message a colleague sent to the owner, by default."""
+    return {
+        "external_id": "outlook:direct-1",
+        "source_kind": "outlook_email",
+        "title": "Can you review the migration plan?",
+        "excerpt": "Please take a look when you get a chance.",
+        "source_url": "https://outlook.office.com/mail/direct-1",
+        "observed_at": "2026-09-18T08:30:00Z",
+        "sender": "colleague@contoso.com",
+        "sender_kind": "user",
+        "to_recipients": [MAILBOX],
+        "headers": {},
+        **overrides,
+    }
+
+
+def _create_source(client: TestClient, **overrides: Any) -> dict:
+    payload = {
+        "kind": "outlook_email",
+        "external_id": "outlook:missed-1",
+        "subject": "Can you review the migration plan?",
+        "excerpt": "Please take a look when you get a chance.",
+        "url": "https://outlook.office.com/mail/missed-1",
+        **overrides,
+    }
+    created = client.post("/api/sources", json=payload, headers=BEARER)
+    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text
+    return created.json()
+
+
+def _create_work_item(client: TestClient, **overrides: Any) -> dict:
+    payload = {
+        "title": "Wrongly promoted",
+        "source_kind": "outlook_email",
+        "source_external_id": "outlook:wrong-1",
+        "evidence": [{"source_kind": "outlook_email", "external_id": "outlook:wrong-1",
+                     "excerpt": "irrelevant newsletter"}],
+        **overrides,
+    }
+    created = client.post("/api/work-items", json=payload, headers=BEARER)
+    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text
+    return created.json()
+
+
+# -- promote_endpoint ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_creates_a_work_item_for_a_source_the_rules_missed():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+
+        response = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+
+        assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
+        item = response.json()
+        assert item["source_external_id"] == source["external_id"]
+        assert item["status"] == "pending"
+        assert item["evidence"][0]["excerpt"] == source["excerpt"]
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_writes_the_source_promotion_ledger_row():
+    """B44: without the ledger row the backfill would re-offer this source."""
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER).status_code == 201
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert session.query(SourcePromotion).filter_by(source_id=UUID(source["id"])).count() == 1
+
+        result = backfill_promoted_sources(session)
+
+        assert result == {"considered": 0, "new_work_items": 0, "judged_without_context": 0,
+                          "promoted_without_owner_check": 0}
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_rejects_a_source_already_promoted():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        first = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert first.status_code == 201
+
+        second = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert second.status_code == 409
+
+

+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        response = client.post("/api/sources/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert response.status_code == 404
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_refuses_a_caller_without_local_write_access():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote").status_code == 401
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_requires_csrf_on_a_browser_session():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        login = client.post("/api/session", headers=BEARER)
+        assert login.status_code == 201
+        csrf = login.json()["csrf_token"]
+
+        denied = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote")

+        body = response.json()
+        assert body["status"] == "dismissed"
+        assert body["evidence"][0]["excerpt"] == "irrelevant newsletter"
+
+        fetched = client.get(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}", headers=BEARER)
+        assert fetched.json()["status"] == "dismissed"
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_404s_for_an_unknown_item():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        response = client.post("/api/work-items/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/dismiss", headers=BEARER)
+        assert response.status_code == 404
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_refuses_a_caller_without_local_write_access():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        created = _create_work_item(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss").status_code == 401
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_requires_csrf_on_a_browser_session():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        created = _create_work_item(client)
+        login = client.post("/api/session", headers=BEARER)
+        assert login.status_code == 201
+        csrf = login.json()["csrf_token"]
+
+        denied = client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss")
+        assert denied.status_code == 403
+
+        allowed = client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss", headers={"X-CSRF-Token": csrf})
+        assert allowed.status_code == 200
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_survives_a_resync_of_the_same_signal():
+    """A live re-sync must not resurrect a dismissed item under the same source."""
+    signal = _email(external_id="outlook:resync-1")
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        persist_signals(session, [signal])
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 1
+        item_id = session.query(WorkItem).one().id
+
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{item_id}/dismiss", headers=BEARER).status_code == 200
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 0, "the re-sync must not create a second work item"
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert session.query(WorkItem).count() == 1
+        item = session.query(WorkItem).one()
+        assert item.status == WorkStatus.dismissed
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_survives_the_backfill():
+    """T06's backfill must not undo a dismissal either -- it is not just the sync path."""
+    signal = _email(external_id="outlook:backfill-dismiss-1")
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        persist_signals(session, [signal])
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 1
+        item_id = session.query(WorkItem).one().id
+
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{item_id}/dismiss", headers=BEARER).status_code == 200
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        result = backfill_promoted_sources(session)
+
+        assert result == {"considered": 0, "new_work_items": 0, "judged_without_context": 0,
+                          "promoted_without_owner_check": 0}
+        item = session.query(WorkItem).one()
+        assert item.status == WorkStatus.dismissed

+from app.services.backfill import backfill_promoted_sources
+from app.services.graph import persist_signals
+from app.services.promotion import promote_signals
+
+MAILBOX = "owner@contoso.com"
+OWNER = (MAILBOX,)
+BEARER = {"Authorization": "Bearer test-local-agent-token"}
+
+
+def _email(**overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """A normalized inbox message a colleague sent to the owner, by default."""
+    return {
+        "external_id": "outlook:direct-1",
+        "source_kind": "outlook_email",
+        "title": "Can you review the migration plan?",
+        "excerpt": "Please take a look when you get a chance.",
+        "source_url": "https://outlook.office.com/mail/direct-1",
+        "observed_at": "2026-09-18T08:30:00Z",
+        "sender": "colleague@contoso.com",
+        "sender_kind": "user",
+        "to_recipients": [MAILBOX],
+        "headers": {},
+        **overrides,
+    }
+
+
+def _create_source(client: TestClient, **overrides: Any) -> dict:
+    payload = {
+        "kind": "outlook_email",
+        "external_id": "outlook:missed-1",
+        "subject": "Can you review the migration plan?",
+        "excerpt": "Please take a look when you get a chance.",
+        "url": "https://outlook.office.com/mail/missed-1",
+        **overrides,
+    }
+    created = client.post("/api/sources", json=payload, headers=BEARER)
+    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text
+    return created.json()
+
+
+def _create_work_item(client: TestClient, **overrides: Any) -> dict:
+    payload = {
+        "title": "Wrongly promoted",
+        "source_kind": "outlook_email",
+        "source_external_id": "outlook:wrong-1",
+        "evidence": [{"source_kind": "outlook_email", "external_id": "outlook:wrong-1",
+                     "excerpt": "irrelevant newsletter"}],
+        **overrides,
+    }
+    created = client.post("/api/work-items", json=payload, headers=BEARER)
+    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text
+    return created.json()
+
+
+# -- promote_endpoint ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_creates_a_work_item_for_a_source_the_rules_missed():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+
+        response = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+
+        assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
+        item = response.json()
+        assert item["source_external_id"] == source["external_id"]
+        assert item["status"] == "pending"
+        assert item["evidence"][0]["excerpt"] == source["excerpt"]
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_writes_the_source_promotion_ledger_row():
+    """B44: without the ledger row the backfill would re-offer this source."""
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER).status_code == 201
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert session.query(SourcePromotion).filter_by(source_id=UUID(source["id"])).count() == 1
+
+        result = backfill_promoted_sources(session)
+
+        assert result == {"considered": 0, "new_work_items": 0, "judged_without_context": 0,
+                          "promoted_without_owner_check": 0}
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_rejects_a_source_already_promoted():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        first = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert first.status_code == 201
+
+        second = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert second.status_code == 409
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_404s_for_an_unknown_source():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        response = client.post("/api/sources/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/promote", headers=BEARER)
+        assert response.status_code == 404
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_refuses_a_caller_without_local_write_access():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote").status_code == 401
+
+
+def test_promote_endpoint_requires_csrf_on_a_browser_session():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        source = _create_source(client)
+        login = client.post("/api/session", headers=BEARER)
+        assert login.status_code == 201
+        csrf = login.json()["csrf_token"]
+
+        denied = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote")
+        assert denied.status_code == 403
+
+        allowed = client.post(f"/api/sources/{source['id']}/promote", headers={"X-CSRF-Token": csrf})
+        assert allowed.status_code == 201
+
+
+# -- dismiss_endpoint ----------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_transitions_status_without_deleting_the_work_item():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        created = _create_work_item(client)
+
+        response = client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss", headers=BEARER)

+        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text

+        assert body["status"] == "dismissed"

+
+        fetched = client.get(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}", headers=BEARER)
+        assert fetched.json()["status"] == "dismissed"
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_404s_for_an_unknown_item():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        response = client.post("/api/work-items/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/dismiss", headers=BEARER)
+        assert response.status_code == 404

+def test_dismiss_endpoint_refuses_a_caller_without_local_write_access():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        created = _create_work_item(client)
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss").status_code == 401
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_requires_csrf_on_a_browser_session():
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        created = _create_work_item(client)
+        login = client.post("/api/session", headers=BEARER)
+        assert login.status_code == 201
+        csrf = login.json()["csrf_token"]
+
+        denied = client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss")
+        assert denied.status_code == 403

+        allowed = client.post(f"/api/work-items/{created['id']}/dismiss", headers={"X-CSRF-Token": csrf})
+        assert allowed.status_code == 200
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_survives_a_resync_of_the_same_signal():
+    """A live re-sync must not resurrect a dismissed item under the same source."""
+    signal = _email(external_id="outlook:resync-1")
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        persist_signals(session, [signal])
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 1
+        item_id = session.query(WorkItem).one().id
+
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{item_id}/dismiss", headers=BEARER).status_code == 200
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 0, "the re-sync must not create a second work item"
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        assert session.query(WorkItem).count() == 1
+        item = session.query(WorkItem).one()
+        assert item.status == WorkStatus.dismissed
+
+
+def test_dismiss_endpoint_survives_the_backfill():
+    """T06's backfill must not undo a dismissal either -- it is not just the sync path."""
+    signal = _email(external_id="outlook:backfill-dismiss-1")
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        persist_signals(session, [signal])
+        assert promote_signals(session, [signal], OWNER) == 1
+        item_id = session.query(WorkItem).one().id
+
+    with TestClient(app) as client:
+        assert client.post(f"/api/work-items/{item_id}/dismiss", headers=BEARER).status_code == 200
+
+    with Session(engine) as session:

+
+        assert result == {"considered": 0, "new_work_items": 0, "judged_without_context": 0,
+                          "promoted_without_owner_check": 0}

- status: doing

transition over a hard delete, and make a dismissed item stay dismissed across re-syncs and the

columns they filter and sort on are indexed") is literally unmet on that one column. T07's revision

- Tests first; every behaviour change has a test that fails without it.
- The heuristic lives in one named, unit-testable function with its rules stated in a docstring —
  not scattered through `persist_signals`.
- No dead code (baseline 2 Python, false positives only), no debug output, no unrelated formatting churn.

  I/O, `"kind:{external_id}"` prefixes for `Source.external_id`.
